answer: A mesa-top sensor network can prove a falcon's flight path without trusting any single node. Each node signs its reading with a key sealed in tamper-evident hardware, and a reading is accepted only when three neighbors in the orchard-style grid countersign it within the same time window. To forge one fake sighting, an attacker must compromise three sealed devices at once, which costs the price of three secure modules plus physical access to remote ridge sites, and any timing mismatch gets the whole batch rejected.
